_note: Past-election sweep, checked 30 October 2026 against live sources.

evidence.summary: Donald Trump won the 5 November 2024 presidential election, 312 electoral votes to 226, carrying all seven swing states and the national popular vote. Major networks called the race early on 6 November.
evidence.rationale: A plain, unconditional call stated as seen, made in April 2024 and again four days out, and it landed. The base rate matters: final forecasts had the race near even with prediction markets leaning Trump, and in April Trump led most swing-state polling, so this was roughly a coin flip called correctly, not a long shot. It is a binary outcome with no detail attached, which is why it is strong as a call but carries little information on its own.

evidence.summary: Lula won the 25 October 2026 runoff with about 51.8 percent of valid votes, a lead of nearly 4.4 million. Flavio Bolsonaro refused to concede and said he would seek annulment. Voting was extended by two hours, which drew criticism, and some voters were moved to paper ballots. No electoral authority or court has found fraud; coverage describes a path to annulment as difficult given the reliability of the voting system.
evidence.rationale: He saw rigging, corruption and sacks of fraudulent paper ballots. What exists is an allegation from the losing side and procedural disruption (the extension and a paper-ballot fallback), not a finding. The losing candidate's claim is not evidence. The ballot-sack detail was told on 26 October, the day after the runoff, while he was showing coverage of the paper-ballot fallback, so it is partly after the fact. Held UNRESOLVED until the annulment challenge is decided; if it is rejected with no fraud found, this is CONTRADICTED.

evidence.summary: The incumbent, Lula, won a fourth term over the conservative Flavio Bolsonaro, 51.7 to 48.3, reversing a first round Bolsonaro had led.
evidence.rationale: He declared change coming to Brazil and was shown to pray for the conservative with a heart like David. The incumbent was re-elected and the conservative lost. The before-the-vote line is a prayer declaration, which under the corpus rule is scored as the outcome it asked for, as the Canada 2025 election was. His 28 October retelling, that he had said the election would be rigged, rests on the allegation, not on any finding.

evidence.summary: Abelardo de la Espriella, the right-wing candidate, won Colombia's 21 June 2026 runoff with 49.66 percent to Ivan Cepeda's 48.7, certified on 24 June.
evidence.rationale: A prayer, not a forecast. The conservative won, but by under one point, the opposite of a landslide. Half the asked-for outcome landed.

evidence.summary: At the 27 October 2026 Knesset election Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 seats and the opposition under Gadi Eisenkot 48, with Arab parties at 19. Neither side has the 61 needed; another election is possible. Netanyahu is alive and his bloc finished first.
evidence.rationale: The scoreable detail is that he saw the leader taken out around the autumn election, which in the December 2025 telling means killed. That has not happened. The window runs to 31 October, so this is held two more days; with no event it becomes EXPIRED_WITHOUT_MATCH. His October tellings of a black swan event and a distraction around the election, with Mossad and the 28th named, have no matching event in the coverage checked.
